item.title: Haaland revels in City's contentious win over United
item.description:
Erling Haaland said it was a "great feeling" to seal Manchester City's controversial 1-0 win at Manchester United on Sunday after the Norway striker's goal survived a contentious VAR review.
With City down to 10 men after Phil Foden's dismissal for kicking Bruno Fernandes, Haaland netted on the hour mark with a close-range finish from Josko Gvardiol's cross.
The goal was initially disallowed for offside but VAR eventually overturned that decision, even though City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position and attempted to reach the ball before Haaland.
Fernandez did not touch the ball so the goal was given, allowing Haaland to celebrate his ninth league strike in Manchester derbies.
"I thought maybe someone flicked it. When I found out no one flicked it, I took it personally that they thought I was offside because I'm never usually offside," Haaland said.
"It's always nice to win football games, but especially with 10 men for 60 minutes at Old Trafford, it's such a nice feeling, especially with the fans at the end.
"To look at all the faces of the supporters at the end is just a great feeling."
City were indebted to Gianluigi Donnarumma for a superb save in the final seconds when he clawed away Bryan Mbeumo's blast from 12 yards.
"What a save from Gianluigi at the end as well. He's like a wolf in the goal, he looks like a wolf anyway," Haaland said.
"He's a madman and to have a guy like that in the goal behind you just makes you feel so much more safe."
Victory extended Enzo Maresca's perfect start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola as City manager.
The Italian ran down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling City fans at full-time.
"I think to win a game with 10 players is already special but it's even more special when it's a derby, Manchester derby, for the fans, for the club, for the players and also for the coaching staff," said Maresca.
"This kind of game, they give boost in all the aspects. Again, winning games with 10 players is already nice and then when it's a derby for the players it's even better."
Maresca has been backed by a record œ460 million splurge on new signings.
The midfield pairing of Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson shone, while Iliman Ndiaye made a massive impact as a second-half substitute.
"That's why they are here, that's why the club made an important effort," added Maresca.

item.title: New coach won't use AI in bid to make South Korea fans happy
item.description:
South Korea's new interim coach Robert Moreno said Monday that he wanted to make fans in the country "happy" after a disastrous World Cup and series of damaging controversies.
Former Spain coach Moreno, who was forced to deny earlier this year that he used ChatGPT to prepare for games, will be in charge for friendly matches in the coming months.
The Korea Football Association (KFA) said he could stay on for the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January-February, "subject to an evaluation".
Moreno named captain Son Heung-min in his squad for four upcoming home friendlies and said he wanted to put a smile back on South Korean fans' faces.
"We're going to try to do our work honestly and with the aim of making all Korean football fans happy," said the 48-year-old, who is the first Spaniard to coach South Korea.
"Good matches, and trying to help the players."
Moreno will lead the team against Ecuador and Uruguay in September and Venezuela and Uzbekistan in October.
South Korea had been without a coach since Hong Myung-bo quit following their shock group-stage exit from the World Cup in North America in June.
Hong's departure did little to quell public outrage over the disappointing campaign and added fuel to pre-existing questions about how he was hired.
Police raided KFA headquarters last month as part of an investigation into Hong's 2024 appointment.
The KFA also apologised for allegations that it provided sexual entertainment for foreign referees.
Moreno named striker Son, now in Major League Soccer with Los Angeles FC, in his first squad along with Atletico Madrid's Lee Kang-in and Bayern Munich's Kim Min-jae.
Hong's decision to leave Son on the bench in the first half for the decisive match against South Africa at the World Cup baffled and angered many supporters.
"We're all aware of Son's versatility," said Moreno.
"For me he can play in three positions."
Moreno also addressed allegations that he used artificial intelligence during his time in charge of Russian club Sochi.
Moreno left the top-flight side in September 2025 after a poor run of results and reports said he had heavily relied on ChatGPT in his role, even using it to decide between potential signings.
Moreno called it "a piece of news that is completely false and went viral".
"Obviously I use technology," he said.
"Anyone who spends 10 minutes looking into it can see that everything has been taken out of context and put together to cause harm."

item.title: Yamal: This year I deserve Ballon d'Or
item.description:
Lamine Yamal believes he and Kylian Mbappe are the two best players in the world and said he deserves to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a trophy-laden year with Barcelona and Spain.
"For me, Mbappe and me, we're the two best players in the world," the 19-year-old Barcelona winger said in an interview on Movistar Plus, excerpts of which were published on Sunday.
"I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I've won," he added.
Yamal helped Barcelona retain La Liga before becoming a world champion with Spain this summer, strengthening his claim for the game's most prestigious individual award.
He had struck a more measured tone at a press conference last Tuesday, saying he believed he had a chance after an "incredible" season but would not beg for votes.
Mbappe, meanwhile, has also made his case for the award in recent days.
The France captain finished as top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup, although Real Madrid failed to win a major trophy.
Yamal's Barcelona and Spain teammate Ousmane Dembele, last year's winner, believes the award should remain with a Paris Saint-Germain player after the French club retained the Champions League.
Bayern Munich striker and England international Harry Kane is also among the favourites to win the award, which will be issued in London on October 26.

item.title: Yamal double helps Barca beat Levante, Atletico triumph
item.description:
Lamine Yamal struck twice to help Barcelona to an exciting 4-2 win at Levante on Sunday in La Liga, extending the Catalans' perfect start to the season.
Hansi Flick's side reestablished their three point lead over Real Madrid at the top of the table, after Los Blancos beat Rayo Vallecano on Saturday.
Atletico Madrid defeated Real Sociedad 3-0 with three late goals to move joint-third.
Xavi Espart opened the scoring for the champions in Valencia with Yamal netting the second and then scoring a penalty early in the second half.
Barca may have a 100 percent record so far from their five games but their defensive frailties were exposed as Ivan Romero and Roger Brugue pulled Levante back into the game in the final stages.
Substitute Karim Adeyemi made the game safe for Barca in stoppage time with a stunning solo goal, breaking through at pace and beating Mathew Ryan.
"It was not our best game of course. We had a great start. In the second half we struggled a little bit," Flick told reporters.
"We have to fight to improve. It's normal, we have situations we have to make better, much better. We'll tell the team and go on to the next match, but with the result I'm happy."
Barcelona defender Eric Garcia said that the team relaxed a bit in the second half and it nearly cost them.
"It was a hard game, we did make it harder for ourselves than it needed to be," Garcia told Movistar.
"But it has to teach us something -- if you give any opponent a bit of breathing room they get on top of you."
The Catalans came flying out of the blocks at the Cituat de Valencia stadium, where Levante were unbeaten in eight matches prior.
The visitors took the lead in the fifth minute, with Levante barely touching the ball before Barca defender Espart found the net.
Barca cut through the middle of Levante's team too easily and the 19-year-old finished from the edge of the box with the help of a slight deflection.
It was Espart's first goal for the club, with the young midfielder brought into the first team this season by Flick and deployed at left-back.
Levante responded with a spell of concerted pressure but Petar Ratkov could not get a proper shot away when well placed and Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia saved well from Brugue.
Levante soon came to regret those spurned chances when Raphinha created Barca's second for teenage star Yamal.
The Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Ryan and squared for Yamal to smash into the empty net in the 19th minute.
Paying the penalty Yamal claimed his second goal soon after the restart, winning and then converting a penalty.
The Spain winger was hacked down by Aissa Mandi and powered the resulting spot kick past Ryan for his seventh goal in four games across all competitions.
Andreas Christensen cleared Romero's bobbling shot off the line but the forward capitalised on an Espart error to score a few minutes later.
Brugue capitalised on a Marc Bernal error to net the second and create a tense finale.
However, former Borussia Dortmund winger Adeyemi ended the hosts' dreams of a point with a dynamic burst through the defence and then a cool finish to match.
Atletico Madrid beat Real Sociedad with a late flurry of goals.
Diego Simeone's side were without Julian Alvarez, who suffered a muscle injury in training on Saturday, but got back to winning ways after their defeat last weekend by Athletic Bilbao.
Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring with a penalty after 84 minutes, before Canada international Jonathan David netted his first goal for the club in the 90th minute.
Giuliano Simeone completed the Rojiblancos' victory deep in stoppage time.
Elsewhere, Celta Vigo were held to a 1-1 home draw by Malaga, while Getafe and Deportivo La Coruna also drew 1-1.

item.title: Zverev holds off Shelton to win US Open title
item.description:
Alexander Zverev held off Ben Shelton to win the US Open on Sunday, capturing the second Grand Slam of his career just months after winning the French Open.
The top-seeded German ruthlessly snuffed out a late surge by Shelton to triumph 6-3, 7-6 (7/2), 5-7, 6-2, crushing the eighth seed's hopes of becoming the first US man in 23 years to win a Grand Slam title.
Zverev expunged the bitter memory of his 2020 US Open defeat, when he was two points from victory before falling to Dominic Thiem in five sets.
It would be six years -- with two major finals disappointments -- before he would break through this season.
"I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said at the trophy presentation.
The 23-year-old Shelton was one month shy of his first birthday when Andy Roddick hoisted the 2003 US Open trophy in the last major triumph for a US man.
Hopes were high that Shelton could end the drought after his epic five-set quarter-final victory over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, and a come-from-behind win over compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals.
But Zverev's all-court excellence proved too much for Shelton, despite the support of a star-studded Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd trying to will the American to victory.
With their backing, Shelton surged in the third set, eliminating the errors that Zverev had ruthlessly exploited.
Serving to extend the set, Zverev fell behind 0-40. Shelton fired long on his first set point but on the second Zverev's forehand volley went wide. Shelton had his first break of the match and they were headed to a fourth set.
Zverev, however, responded immediately and decisively, breaking Shelton in the first game of the fourth set and rolling home.
He lifted his arms in triumph after Shelton fired a serve return long on match point and finally received his own huge cheer from the crowd -- but not before some prompting.
Zverev said he didn't initially realize he'd won because he had lost track of the score.
"I knew I broke him twice, but I thought it was 5-1 instead of 6-2, which helped me in a way, because I didn't really get nervous serving out the match," Zverev said.
"In that moment I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all. Then also, of course, when the crowd is loud, it's impossible to hear the umpire, so I didn't hear that she said, 'Game, set, match.'"
Zverev had followed up his French Open victory with a runner-up finish at Wimbledon.
But his New York prospects had looked bleak as he labored through two five-setters to start the tournament.
Now the 29-year-old ranked second in the world has a chance to challenge for the number one ranking with Italian Jannik Sinner currently sidelined by a knee injury.
With this win, Zverev said he might consider himself the best player in the world "right, right now."
"If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead."

item.title: Mojo stands beside Nepal flood victims with Tk35 lakh aid
item.description:
Mojo has always been committed to standing beside people in times of need.
Beyond being a part of people’s everyday moments, supporting communities during crises and humanitarian disasters remains one of Mojo’s core commitments.
Continuing this tradition of humanitarian support, Mojo has extended its support to neighboring Nepal.
Sudden flooding in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers along the Nepal-Tibet border has severely affected several parts of Nepal.
The powerful currents of the mountain rivers have swept away numerous homes, while many people remain missing. Families who have lost loved ones and their homes are now facing deep uncertainty and hardship.
The crisis in the neighboring country has touched the hearts of people across Bangladesh.
Mojo believes that geographical boundaries should never stand in the way of standing beside people during difficult times.
Supporting those affected by such devastating circumstances is a humanitarian responsibility that Mojo considers an integral part of its commitment to society.
To support emergency relief and rehabilitation efforts for people affected and displaced by the sudden floods and landslides, Mojo has donated Tk35 lakh to the Nepal Embassy in Dhaka.
The donation cheque was formally handed over at the Embassy of Nepal.

item.title: UCB, Chartered Life Insurance to revolutionize premium collection via digital channels
item.description:

The agreement was signed by Sufia Akter, deputy managing director, wholesale banking, UCB, and Mohammed Amdad Ullah, acting chief executive officer, Chartered Life Insurance Company PLC.

This partnership reinforces UCB’s commitment to delivering integrated Transaction Banking solutions that create greater value for corporate customers and their stakeholders, in line with the spirit of “One Bank, One Team.”

item.title: NCC Bank, GP to accelerate smart banking 4.0 and tech innovations
item.description:
NCC Bank PLC and Grameenphone Ltd. are working on a strategic partnership to drive digital transformation, enhance technological capabilities, and ensure innovative digital services for NCC Bank’s customers.
This potential collaboration will focus on digital payments, technology-driven financial services, customer experience enhancement, and various initiatives supporting Bangladesh's journey toward a cashless economy.
Recently, at a meeting held at Grameenphone's head office, NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin and Grameenphone CEO Yasir Azman led their respective delegations.
Discussions covered the strategic goals, technological capabilities, digital ecosystems, and potential areas of collaboration for both organizations.
Representing NCC Bank were additional managing director Md Zakir Anam, deputy managing director Md Habibur Rahman, SVP & head of ICT Md Sajjadul Islam, and unit head, retail & DFS business unit SM Tanvir Hasan.
Representing Grameenphone were head of large accounts M Shaon Azad, head of large account 4 Mahbubur Rahman, key account manager Sumaiya Tarannum, head of product, partnership & operations Md Mahbubul Alam Bhuiyan, along with other senior officials from both organizations.
During the meeting, discussions focused on creating new opportunities by integrating Grameenphone's extensive digital ecosystem and technological capabilities with NCC Bank's banking expertise and financial service strengths.
Potential areas of collaboration include innovative digital products and services, digital payment solutions, joint digital initiatives and campaigns, and customer-centric technology-driven financial services.
This partnership is expected to ensure a smoother, safer, and more seamless banking and digital payment experience, while also playing a positive role in advancing Bangladesh's digital financial inclusion and cashless economy.
In this regard, NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin said : "This collaboration with Grameenphone further strengthens NCC Bank's commitment to delivering world-class banking services. item.title: Bangladesh suffer 10-0 defeat to North Korea in Asian Games opener
item.description:
Bangladesh suffered a heavy 10-0 defeat to North Korea in their opening match of the Asian Games women’s football tournament on Monday, with the formidable North Korean side scoring seven times in the first half.
Bangladesh struggled to cope with North Korea’s pace and attacking pressure as the East Asian side raced into a commanding lead before the break.
North Korea added three more goals after halftime to complete a 10-0 victory, making a strong statement at the start of their Asian Games campaign.
The North Koreans, who have enjoyed considerable success at youth level, are among the favourites for the women’s football gold medal in Japan.
Striker Ri Song A, who was born and raised in Japan, was in North Korea’s starting line-up and also found the net in the second half.
Several hundred pro-Pyongyang supporters, many dressed in red, created a lively atmosphere in Osaka as they sang and chanted throughout the match.
The North Korean teams were welcomed by supporters waving flags when they arrived for the Games last week, wearing white blazers and pink ties.
More than 100 North Korean athletes are competing in 14 sports at the Games, which are being held in Nagoya-Aichi and officially open on September 19.
North Korea suspended participation in international sporting competitions during the pandemic but returned to the Asian Games at Hangzhou in 2023 and also competed at the Paris Olympics.
North Korea's women's team will next face South Korea in a Group F clash on September 21.
The North Korean men's team will begin their campaign against China on Wednesday.

item.title: Dhaka sees rise in unclaimed bodies
item.description:
No one comes looking for them. They have no relatives and no claimants. After lying in morgue refrigerators for days, they are eventually dubbed “unclaimed” bodies.
The number of such unclaimed bodies is increasing at an alarming rate in Dhaka.
Recently, the dismembered body of an unidentified woman and the bodies of two unidentified people were recovered from the capital’s National Eidgah and Supreme Court areas.
Those concerned said the rise is linked not only to deaths caused by accidents and among floating people, but also to the silent fate of numerous unidentified people who fall victim to murder.
Experts said a lack of professionalism among law enforcement agencies, an integrated database, the use of technology in crime-prone areas, police sources, modern DNA identification systems and effective state initiatives are among the reasons many bodies cannot be returned to their relatives.
According to Anjuman Mufidul Islam, 2,104 unclaimed bodies were buried between January 2023 and August 2026.
Of these, 490 were buried in 2023, 570 in 2024, 644 in 2025 and 400 up to August 2026.
The figures show a rising trend in the number of unclaimed bodies in the capital.
Kamrul Ahmed, burial service officer at Anjuman Mufidul Islam, told Dhaka Tribune on Monday morning that the organization receives bodies from hospitals with the necessary documents before taking them to cemeteries.
Most of the bodies are buried at Jurain and Rayerbazar Martyred Intellectuals Cemetery, he said.
Unclaimed bodies are buried at Jurain Cemetery under Dhaka South City Corporation and at the cemetery adjacent to the Rayerbazar Martyred Intellectuals Memorial under Dhaka North City Corporation.
There had been complications over space for burying the bodies, resulting in many unclaimed bodies remaining in morgues for extended periods.
Kamrul said the problem had caused difficulties in burying the bodies for a long time but has now been resolved.
Three unidentified bodies were recovered in the capital on September 12.
The dismembered body of a teenage girl was recovered from a schoolbag that had floated into the Hakkarpar canal in Adabor.
On the same day, police recovered the bodies of two unidentified people from footpaths near the National Eidgah ground and the High Court Mazar. One was approximately 65 years old and the other 45.
Adabor police station Officer-in-Charge Zahidul Islam Jahangir told Dhaka Tribune that four pieces of the teenage girl’s body were recovered from a schoolbag in the canal around 5pm on Saturday.
Eighteen hours later, her two legs were recovered.
The girl was between 14 and 16 years old, but her identity has not yet been established.
The OC said police collected her fingerprints and checked them against the National Identity Card (NID) database. However, as she did not have an NID, no matching information was found.
The dismembered body has been kept at the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College.
Police filed a murder case with Adabor police station as the complainant over the incident.
Meanwhile, the bodies of two unidentified people were recovered from footpaths near the National Eidgah ground and High Court Mazar on the same day.
Shahbagh police station Officer-in-Charge Moniruzzaman told Dhaka Tribune on Monday afternoon that police recovered the bodies based on information provided by pedestrians.
The identity of one of the men has been established. His name is Jewel and his home is in Lalbagh. The identity of the other person remains unknown.
Police said unidentified bodies whose identities can be established are disposed of according to the law and handed over to their relatives.
Bodies that remain unidentified and unclaimed often stay in morgues. In such cases, police take the necessary measures according to court directives.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Deputy Commissioner (Media) Md Akter Hossain told Dhaka Tribune on Monday evening that police had no information indicating that the number of unclaimed bodies had increased.
“We do not have such information. The information you have received is your analysis, but we also need to know whether it has increased,” he said.
Touhidul Haque, an associate professor at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research at Dhaka University, told Dhaka Tribune that an increase in unclaimed bodies indicates that the law and order situation is not normal.
Criminals are taking advantage of gaps in the efficiency and professionalism of law enforcement agencies, he said.
“They have realized that they can commit crimes and get away with them. As a result, the number of unclaimed bodies is increasing,” he said.
Touhidul said criminals are dismembering bodies after murder, putting them in bags and floating them in water, making identification difficult.
“Unclaimed bodies are increasing for various reasons, including murder. Police have not been able to demonstrate the necessary efficiency to control this,” he said.
The crime expert said the shortcomings of the police must first be acknowledged and addressed at the state level.
Crime-prone areas need to be identified, technology should be deployed in those areas and police sources need to be developed, he said.
“This will make it easier to arrest criminals. Besides, if they are brought under the law and strict punishment is ensured, crime will decrease,” he added.

item.title: Rohingyas struggle with 20 litres of water per person
item.description:
At 2:40pm, Ashraf arrives at a tap stand in the market area of Camp-22 in Teknaf with a large water container. After filling it, he carries the water through hilly and uneven paths to his hut, a journey that takes seven to eight minutes.
He carries containers on both shoulders and in his hands.
Ashraf lives with his elderly parents and four siblings, making the daily collection of water his responsibility.
“Whether I am healthy or sick, I have to collect water. My body aches from carrying it. We are given 20 litres of water per person for drinking, cooking, bathing and sanitation. But 20 litres is nowhere near enough,” Ashraf said.
“One can go without a meal, but one cannot go without water. We cannot pour extra water after using the toilet, so foul smells remain. This is how we are living,” he said.
The situation becomes worse during the dry season. On rainy days, there is some flexibility, but in the dry season, even getting 20 litres becomes difficult. As a result, many have to bathe once every three or four days.
“If we use water for bathing, there is no water left for cooking or other urgent needs,” Ashraf said.
He credited Oxfam’s water supply system with reducing their suffering. Previously, residents had to collect water from distant locations, and women often faced harassment while traveling to and from those places.
“It is not possible to live amid so much hardship. We want to return to our own country,” Ashraf said.
At the same tap stand, Ayesha arrives with her eight-year-old daughter. Her husband is sick, so she collects water for the family every day. It takes about five minutes to walk from their home to the tap stand.
Ayesha has two daughters, one son and a sick husband. Carrying all the water alone is difficult, so she sometimes brings her daughter with her.
“Twenty litres per person is not enough for cooking, eating and bathing. The supply decreases during the dry season. We cannot bathe every day. One person has to bathe one day and another the next,” she said.
During a visit to her home, half-washed pots and utensils could be seen. Ayesha said the lack of water means the dishes cannot always be kept clean.
“We wash them when we cook,” she said.
DSK Assistant Engineer Fazlul Karim said DSK and Oxfam have been jointly working to ensure safe water in Rohingya camps since 2017.
He said the biggest challenge in Teknaf is groundwater. At a depth of 20 to 30 feet, there are layers of stones and rocks, making it difficult to extract sufficient water.
The camp requires about 500,000 litres of water a day, which is why a surface water treatment plant has been established.
The biggest challenge comes during the dry season. From December, canal water begins to decline for the next five months. During this period, water is collected through a pipeline from an area about 5km away, where there are no residents and only a few farmers cultivate land.
The muddy water is first clarified using alum and then disinfected with chlorine. The water is subsequently tested at the plant’s own laboratory. According to WHO standards, residual chlorine should remain between 0.2 and 0.5mg per litre.
Water quality is tested at the treatment plant, tap stands and households. A third-party monitoring team also regularly tests water samples. Two to three checkers and a hygiene team work in the field every day.
From the treatment plant, water is sent to a second storage tank before being distributed through four blocks to 137 tap stands. Water is distributed at 7am and 2:40pm every day.
Three separate tap stands serve the host community, providing safe water to 693 local residents.
When the canal dries up, the per-person water supply falls from 20 litres to 15 litres. The WASH sector says the supply should never fall below 10 litres per person. So far, however, the supply has not dropped to that level, with the minimum remaining at 15 litres.
Host community residents also had to collect water from distant locations before Oxfam’s treatment plant was established.
Local beneficiaries said people were previously reluctant to marry their daughters into the area because women faced harassment while collecting water in the early morning and evening.
The nearby tap stands, which provide water twice a day, have now reduced the hardship faced by local residents.
RRRC Md Mizanur Rahman said the biggest challenge is maintaining the services that already exist.
The Rohingya population is increasing for two reasons. Conflict across the border continues to drive new arrivals, while around 225,000 children have been born in the camps over the past nine years.
At the same time, international funding is declining.
Maintaining food, education, health and infrastructure services has become increasingly difficult. Many organizations are winding down projects as funding comes to an end, while assistance from UN agencies has also decreased.
Mizanur Rahman warned that if the trend continues, even ensuring the minimum food supply could become difficult in 2027.
He said further cuts in services could also make law and order a major challenge.
Bangladesh cannot bear the expenses of supporting 1.2 million people from another country over the long term while also struggling to improve the living standards of its own population.

item.title: Ducsu faces backlash over Jinnah photos in archive, DU admin cites university law violation
item.description:
The reopening of Dhaka University’s Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) archive with photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah has drawn protests, including the smashing and tearing of the images, as well as objections from student organizations and the university administration.
Ducsu Secretary for Liberation War and Democratic Movement Affairs Fatima Tasnim Zuma inaugurated the renovated archive on Sunday alongside VP Shadik Kayem and GS S M Farhad.
Three Jinnah-related images were included: a 1948 photograph of Jinnah declaring Urdu the sole state language of Pakistan at what was then the Racecourse Ground; a photograph from the All India Muslim League’s 1940 Lahore session; and a Dawn newspaper clipping on the 1970 election.
The display included no solo or prominent photograph of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, although a photograph of his sons’ 1974 weddings and three newspaper clippings mentioning him remained.
At around 2pm yesterday, Muhammad Abu Tayab, also known as Habilder, a student of DU’s Urdu Department and the oldest candidate in the last Ducsu election, entered the archive and physically destroyed a solo photograph of Jinnah, tearing it from its frame.
He argued that no one should be allowed to act unilaterally and questioned whether Ducsu’s manifesto had promised to elevate Jinnah as a hero, referring to the memories of 1971 and the Language Movement. Chhatra Federation’s DU unit then handed him a Dawn clipping featuring Jinnah, which Tayab also destroyed.
Chhatra Federation leader Arko Barua defended the act, echoing Zuma’s own justification for displaying the photographs — that she had put them up because she “wanted to” — and said they tore them down for the same reason.
Barua later installed a photograph of Ghulam Azam, the former Jamaat-e-Islami ameer convicted by the International Crimes Tribunal in 2013 of crimes against humanity, in the same archive space.
The photograph, captioned with an account of Azam being beaten by a crowd outside Baitul Mukarram on January 1, 1981, was explicitly presented by Barua as mirroring Zuma’s rationale: if she could add Jinnah’s photograph on personal impulse, he could add Azam’s in the same way.
When approached for comment, Zuma told Dhaka Tribune that the images were similar to those in the “Bangladesh O Bishwo Porichoy” textbook and had been displayed with explanatory captions to document DU’s history from 1905 to 1971, rather than to honor Jinnah.
She said she was not responsible for resolving why other removed “icons of fascism” had not been reinstated, referring the matter to the state level.
Ducsu GS Farhad similarly defended the display, saying that including Jinnah’s Urdu declaration was intended to present his stance against Bangladesh, not celebrate it. Omitting that history, he said, would effectively favor Jinnah.
Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal condemned the display before the physical protest, linking it to a separate controversy over the renaming of Madhur Canteen as “Ishrat Manzil” as evidence that Ducsu was drifting away from the university’s liberation-era spirit towards “love for Pakistan.”
Shortly after the Jinnah photographs were smashed and torn, the university administration, in a statement issued by its Public Relations Office, said several Ducsu actions had violated university law.
These included the unauthorized installation of a “Nirbhik July” memorial near the Ducsu building on without approval from the Syndicate or VC; the display of photographs of Jinnah and former Chhatra Sangha leader Abdul Malek, which the administration described as “incompatible” with the history of the Language Movement and the country’s independence; and the launch of an unauthorized teacher-evaluation website accused of exposing personal data and duplicating an already approved university policy.
VC Dr ABM Obaidul Islam told Dhaka Tribune: “Ducsu acted against university law.”
The Dhaka University authorities warned Ducsu against creating any “parallel” administrative structure, threatening disciplinary action over several recent initiatives that they say violated university rules and bypassed its administrative authority.
In a statement issued yesterday, the university raised objections to an unauthorized July uprising memorial erected by Ducsu, the display of photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Abdul Malek in the Ducsu gallery, and the launch of a separate website for evaluating university teachers.
The authorities said there was “no scope for establishing a dual administration” at the university and that Ducsu, despite being an important representative body of students, must conduct its activities within the university’s existing laws, rules, policies and administrative framework.
“Any attempt to establish a parallel structure or process by bypassing the university’s administrative authority will be strictly resisted,” the statement said.
Members of the University Teachers’ Network visited the Ducsu archive yesterday afternoon after the Jinnah photographs were broken. Among those present were Professor Dr Samina Luthfa of the Department of Sociology and Professor Dr Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan of the Department of International Relations.
In a press release issued around 4pm, Bangladesh Students’ Union (a faction) expressed deep concern and outrage over the display of Jinnah’s photographs at the archive.
Its president Tamzid Haider Chanchol and general secretary Shimul Kumbhkar said: “The people of this land have a long and bloody history of struggle against Pakistani rule and exploitation. When Muhammad Ali Jinnah came to Dhaka in March 1948 and declared Urdu as the sole state language of Pakistan, the student community of this country protested against him right then. That protest later took the shape of a broader national liberation struggle through the Language Movement. On 21 February 1952, the sacrifices of countless people, including Salam, Barkat, Rafiq and Jabbar, created a new history in the struggle to establish the right to language.”
Another faction of the Bangladesh Students’ Union, aligned with the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB), held a separate press briefing on the issue.
Mahir Shahriar Reza, president of the faction, urged the university administration to restore all the “glorious aspects that existed before” while removing the “controversial items” that Islami Chhatra Shibir had added to the archive.

item.title: Bangladesh’s elusive No 9: Dooley searches far and wide
item.description:
When Thomas Dooley first saw Japan-based Shuki Itofusa, the Bangladesh coach had one pressing question: could he play as a No 9?
Shuki nodded. With his limited English, however, he had not fully understood what Dooley was asking.
It did not take long for the coach to discover the answer. Shuki could impress on the wing, but he was not the specialist centre-forward Bangladesh desperately needed.
Another name was effectively crossed off Dooley’s list of potential No 9s.
For the German-American coach, finding that elusive striker has emerged as one of the biggest challenges as Bangladesh prepare for the Fifa Asean Cup in Indonesia and, beyond that, the Saff Championship on home soil in November.
It is hardly a new problem.
Bangladesh have produced goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and wingers, but a reliable international-level centre-forward has remained difficult to find.
Successive coaches have resorted to makeshift solutions, deploying false nines or moving players from other positions into the centre of attack.
Sajjad Hossain, Sumon Reza, Shahriar Emon, Rakib Hossain, Sheikh Morsalin and Rafiqul Islam have all been tried in attacking roles at different times.
None has yet established himself as the consistent goalscorer the national side has been searching for.
Even Sumon, a recognised striker in domestic football, struggled to translate his club form into a sustained impact for Bangladesh.
Dooley has inherited the same problem.
His first match in charge provided a striking illustration.
Bangladesh beat San Marino 2-1 in June, but both goals came from centre-back Topu Barman rather than a striker.
The search has continued during preparations for the Fifa Asean Cup.
Dooley has experimented with available attacking options during training and practice matches, including the game against Fortis, while assessing overseas-based footballers who could strengthen his squad.
“We need a ‘Number Nine,’ but finding one is extremely difficult,” Dooley said.
“I’ve spoken to a few candidates, but they can’t leave college to come and play. We are searching everywhere.”
Dooley’s search has extended well beyond Bangladesh.
One player on his radar is US-based Ronan Sullivan, who previously impressed for Bangladesh at youth level.
Louis Watson has also attracted interest, but neither is currently available.
Dooley acknowledged that having such players would make his task easier, but said recruiting overseas footballers of Bangladeshi descent was far more complicated than supporters might assume.
“Yes, it would have been much easier if Louis Watson and the Sullivan brothers had joined us. But they aren’t coming,” he said.
Academic commitments, club responsibilities and personal circumstances can all prevent overseas-based players from joining the national setup even when they are eligible and interested.
Shuki is among several overseas-based players Dooley has assessed during the current camp.
The Japan-based winger survived the latest squad cut as Dooley reduced the preliminary Asean Cup group, but his strengths appear to lie elsewhere rather than filling the vacancy at centre-forward.
The coach nevertheless has considerably greater quality available elsewhere in the squad, with overseas-based players adding competition across different positions.
Yet that has not resolved the question at the sharp end of the attack.
Bangladesh will travel to Indonesia for the Fifa Asean Cup, where they have been drawn alongside hosts Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
The tournament runs from September 24 to October 4 and will serve as a major part of their preparation for November’s Saff Championship in Dhaka.
For Dooley, Saff remains the bigger target. He has previously described the home championship as Bangladesh’s most important tournament.
And before it arrives, one question remains unanswered: who will score the goals?
If Dooley can finally find a genuine No 9, at home or among the Bangladeshi diaspora, the answer could significantly change Bangladesh’s prospects.

item.title: Several injured as fire triggers panic at MMCH
item.description:
Several people were injured while rushing to evacuate after a fire broke out in an elevator of the new building at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital on Monday evening.
The fire broke out around 6pm, Mymensingh Sadar Fire Service Station Officer Julhaz Uddin told Dhaka Tribune.
He said a unit from the Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU) Fire Station responded after receiving the report and brought the fire under control. However, heavy smoke was still coming out of the elevator.
“The immediate cause of the fire is not known. However, chaos was created as people rushed to come down, and several people were injured after falling,” Julhaz said.
He added that another team from the Sadar Fire Station was on its way to the hospital and that the cause of the fire would be determined after it was completely brought under control.
Hospital Assistant Director (Administration) Dr Mohammad Main Uddin Khan said the fire was initially believed to have originated from the elevator machinery.
“The situation at the hospital is currently completely normal. Medical services are also continuing normally,” he said.
He said an investigation committee would be formed to determine the actual cause of the fire and the extent of the damage.

item.title: Ex-army chief Shafiuddin seeks 30 days to appear before ACC
item.description:
Former army chief General (retd) S M Shafiuddin Ahmed sought 30 days’ time to appear before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to give his statement in an investigation into allegations of acquiring illegal wealth through corruption and irregularities.
He was scheduled to appear and give his statement at the ACC headquarters in Segunbagicha in the capital on Monday. The next course of action on the appeal of seeking time will be taken in accordance with the law, said Akhtarul Islam, deputy director of the ACC’s Public Relations Division.
Akhtarul Islam said, “He (ex-army chief) was scheduled to appear before the ACC on Monday to give his statement. He has sought 30 days’ time and the next course of action will be taken according to the law.”
Earlier, the ACC served a notice to General (retd) S M Shafiuddin Ahmed to record his statement as part of the investigation into the allegations. The notice, signed by Commission Director Md Abul Hasnat, asked him to appear at the ACC headquarters at 12:30 pm on Monday. The notice said that hearing and recording his statement regarding the allegations was “essential” for the sake of a proper investigation.

item.title: Jamaat ameer accuses BNP of forgetting its pledge to institutionalize democracy
item.description:
Leader of the Opposition Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Monday accused the ruling BNP of forgetting its pledge to institutionalize democracy, saying the July 2024 mass uprising created a historic opportunity to establish democracy in the country.
“The previous Awami fascist government had buried democracy, but the July 2024 mass uprising created a historic opportunity to establish democracy in the country. Before the election, BNP pledged to institutionalize democracy. But after coming to power, they have forgotten that pledge,” he said in a message issued ahead of International Democracy Day, to be observed on Tuesday.
Shafiqur, also ameer of the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, said the previous Awami League government deprived people of their voting rights, justice, social security and fundamental rights.
“Democracy is not merely a temporary process of forming a government; rather, it is the main foundation for ensuring people’s fundamental rights, social justice, freedom of expression and the rule of law,” he said.
If democracy remains protected, a society can move forward on the path of progress, free from authoritarianism, exploitation and discrimination, the opposition leader said.
He said Bangladesh has a long history of sacrifice and struggle, with people repeatedly shedding blood to restore democracy and human rights.
“Unfortunately, throughout history, the democratic rights of the people have been taken away in various ways due to authoritarian attitudes and abuse of power,” Shafiqur said.
He said students and people from all walks of life brought the July uprising by shedding their blood.
“This uprising must not be allowed to fail. At any cost, we must build a discrimination-free and humane Bangladesh that meets the expectations of the nation,” the opposition leader said.
He said there is no alternative to democracy in building a discrimination-free society based on justice, honesty and human values.
“On this special occasion of International Democracy Day, Jamaat pledges to consolidate and institutionalise democracy. To this end, Jamaat has been working tirelessly to establish equality, the rule of law, citizens’ rights and freedom of expression in the country,” Shafiqur said.
“The nation must not be pushed towards the curses of enforced disappearances, killings and crossfire under any circumstances,” he added.
The opposition leader called for implementing the referendum verdict to free the administration from narrow partisan and for making the country free from bribery, corruption, extortion and land grabbing.
“We must pledge to build a completely transparent and genuinely people-oriented system of governance,” he said.
Shafiqur called upon people from all walks of life to play a united role in institutionalising democracy, ensuring fair civic services and standing against any form of injustice to build a discrimination-free and humane Bangladesh.

item.title: Five bodies recovered in Dhaka, police suspect vagrants
item.description:
Police recovered the bodies of five people, including a woman, from separate locations in the capital on Monday. None of the deceased could be identified.
The bodies were taken to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsies.
A 45-year-old unidentified man was found dead beside a road near Araf Car Wash in the Shanir Akhra U-turn area of Jatrabari.
In Motijheel, an unidentified man, around 50, was found lying unconscious on the road opposite Notre Dame College. A pharmaceutical company representative, Nasir, found him and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital on Monday morning. He died at around 11am while undergoing treatment.
Nasir said he believed the man had died from illness and lack of food.
Meanwhile, an unidentified woman, around 30, was found in an ailing condition near Dhaka Medical College Hospital under Shahbagh police station. Hospital staff rescued her and admitted her on Monday morning. She died at around 11:15am while undergoing treatment, said acting ward master Ayub Ali.
In Kamrangirchar, police recovered the body of an unidentified 65-year-old man from the Jauyahati area on Monday morning, said SI Praneshwar Das, duty officer of the police station.
Locals said the man frequently roamed the area and was known to them, but they did not know his identity. He was believed to be a vagrant.
Separately, Shahbagh police recovered the body of an unidentified man, around 30, from a roadside pavement near the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery. SI Bijoy Mondal recovered the body, which was later taken to the DMCH morgue.
Police suspected that the man was also a vagrant.

item.title: PM stresses political, economic empowerment for sustainable democracy
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday called for ensuring people’s political and economic empowerment to make democracy sustainable and establish it on a strong institutional foundation.
“Democratic rights are not limited to exercising the right to vote. To make democracy sustainable and establish it on an institutional foundation, it is essential to ensure the political and economic empowerment of the people,” he said in a message on the occasion of International Day of Democracy.
The prime minister said his government is committed to restoring the religious, political, social and cultural rights of the people.
Greeting democracy-loving people in Bangladesh and across the world, he expressed his support for their democratic and human rights.
Tarique Rahman said democratic rights had been taken away and democracy had been “killed” in Bangladesh at different times since independence.
Recalling the role of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman, he said the late President, who declared Bangladesh’s independence, had introduced multiparty democracy in the country and restored freedom of speech, individual liberty and freedom of the press.
“Whether in government or in opposition, BNP has repeatedly stood for democracy from every position,” the Prime Minister said. He said the country had witnessed the establishment of what he described as a fascist system of rule and exploitation after the people’s democratic and political rights were taken away.
Tarique Rahman said the student-led mass movement, following more than one and a half decades of movements and struggles, ended the fascist rule in the country through a bloody mass uprising.
“In a fascism-free Bangladesh, the people entrusted the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) with the responsibility of running the state through a free, fair and neutral election,” he said.
The prime minister said the fundamental philosophy of democracy is to establish people’s freedom of speech and individual liberty, equality, human dignity and social justice in the state and society.

item.title: 10 students injured in clash at JU
item.description:
Students of Jahangirnagar University’s (JU) Rabindranath Tagore Hall and Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall clashed on Monday, leaving at least 10 students injured.
The clash began around 3pm on a road adjacent to Rabindranath Tagore Hall.
Witnesses said the dispute stemmed from a longstanding disagreement over the ownership of six shops located in front of Nazrul Hall.
Students of Nazrul Hall have been demanding ownership of the shops, arguing that they are located in the area adjacent to their hall. Students of Rabindranath Tagore Hall, however, said the shops had been under their hall’s jurisdiction since before Nazrul Hall was established. They accused Nazrul Hall students of attempting to take control of the shops forcibly.
The dispute escalated into an altercation and later a clash between the two groups.
University administration and members of the proctorial body rushed to the scene and tried to bring the situation under control. The students eventually dispersed and returned to their respective halls.
JU Assistant Proctor Dr Abdus Sattar Joy said the situation was now calm. “Both groups have been sent back to their respective halls. The two hall administrations and the university administration will discuss the issue and reach a logical solution,” he said.

item.title: Four children die in Sylhet with suspected measles symptoms
item.description:
Four children died in Sylhet over the past 24 hours while undergoing treatment with suspected measles symptoms, taking the number of deaths from measles and suspected measles complications in the division this year to 164.
Another 146 patients with suspected measles were admitted to hospitals during the same period, according to a report issued by the office of the divisional director of health in Sylhet on Monday.
Of the newly admitted patients, 67 were taken to Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital and 60 to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital. A total of 495 suspected measles patients are currently receiving treatment at hospitals across the division.
The four children who died were Emran Hossain, from Kanaighat, Obaidullah, seven months, from Zakiganj, Safayet, 10 months, from Bahubal in Habiganj and Khadija, aged three years and three months, from Jagannathpur in Sunamganj.
Emran died at Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital, while the other three died at Osmani Medical College Hospital. The number of confirmed measles cases in the division has reached 1,044.
Dr Mohammad Nur-e-Alam Shamim, assistant director for disease control at the Sylhet health department, said there had been no deaths in the previous three days. He said all four victims had other illnesses and that health authorities were taking measures to control the outbreak.
“Patients should be treated at upazila health complexes unless their condition is serious. Those in critical condition should be referred to hospitals in the city,” he said.
He also urged people to seek treatment locally when possible, saying overcrowding at major city hospitals was increasing the risk of transmission. “There is no alternative to public awareness to bring the situation under control,” he added.

item.title: City polls: Jamaat picks Selim Uddin for DNCC, Shadik Kayem for DSCC
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has selected Mohammad Selim Uddin, ameer of its Dhaka North City unit, as its candidate for Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) Vice President (VP) Shadik Kayem for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC), in the next city corporation elections.
Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar disclosed the names while talking to reporters after a Seerat-un-Nabi (PBUH) conference organized by the National Doctors Forum at the Institution of Diploma Engineers, Bangladesh auditorium in the capital.
He said Jamaat is an election-oriented political party and has taken organizational preparations for the upcoming local government elections.
"We have reached the final stage of completing the nomination process for candidates in all Union Parishads, Upazila Parishads, municipalities and city corporations at the grassroots level. In many places, we have already internally announced our candidates," Porwar said.
He said Jamaat will participate in the elections to the two Dhaka city corporations and has already selected its candidates through its organisational process.
"We will officially announce the candidates at the appropriate time. It has already appeared in the media that we have announced Selim Uddin as our candidate in Dhaka North and Shadik Kayem in Dhaka South," he said.
Meanwhile, Shadik Kayem, whose actual name is Md Abu Shadik Kayem, played an important role as a coordinator during the 2024 mass uprising.
He was later elected Ducsu VP in the September 2025 election.
Earlier, the National Citizen Party (NCP) announced its mayoral candidates for the two Dhaka city corporations.
It picked its Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary as its candidate for the DSCC and Spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain as its candidate for the DNCC.
Meanwhile, the ruling BNP has yet to announce its candidates for the city polls.

item.title: Avery Dennison opens smart warehouse to boost apparel competitiveness
item.description:
Avery Dennison has opened a new Smart Warehouse at the Dhaka Export Processing Zone (DEPZ) in Savar, expanding its use of automation and digital technology to support manufacturers serving global apparel and footwear markets.
The 830-square-meter facility features seven automated guided vehicles (AGVs), connected packing software and a warehouse management system, with storage capacity for 25,000 cartons.
According to Avery Dennison, the connected packing system optimizes workflow and enables 72% faster processing. The facility is also designed to handle a fivefold increase in inbound volume compared with the previous capacity, double outbound velocity and increase inventory density by 50%.
The facility is part of Avery Dennison’s broader Manufacturing 4.0 initiative in Bangladesh.
US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T Christensen attended the opening, along with Executive Chairman of the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) Major General Mohammad Moazzem Hossain, ndc, afwc, psc, G, MPhil; President of the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) Syed Mohammad Kamal; and Avery Dennison’s executive leadership team.
The facility was developed in response to rising demand for faster fulfillment, greater customization and more transparent supply chains.
Avery Dennison said fragmented workflows and delays in inventory data had previously contributed to picking delays and logistics inefficiencies, prompting the move toward a more integrated digital warehouse operation.
“Congratulations to Avery Dennison on the opening of its new Smart Warehouse in Bangladesh. This investment is an excellent example of American business, technology, and innovation strengthening the commercial relationship between our two countries,” Ambassador Christensen said.
“Avery Dennison has been a valued member of the BEPZA since 2003. Over the years, the company has made a remarkable contribution to the readymade garment and textile industry,” Major General Mohammad Moazzem Hossain said.
“Avery Dennison is not simply bringing investment to Bangladesh; it is also bringing technology, knowledge and modern production practices. Technology transfer and the development of a skilled local workforce are among the most valuable long-term benefits that foreign direct investment can bring to a developing economy,” he said.
Michael Barton, senior vice president and general manager, Apparel Solutions, Solutions Group, Avery Dennison, emphasized the company’s long-term commitment to Bangladesh.
“Bangladesh is an important part of our global apparel business. We are fully committed to growing alongside the industry here. As customer requirements become faster, more customized and more data-driven, the infrastructure supporting apparel production must evolve as well. This facility brings together automation, connected systems and our teams’ expertise to strengthen the speed and reliability with which we serve customers,” Barton said.
Sazzad Hossain, general manager, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, Apparel Solutions, Solutions Group, Avery Dennison, said accuracy and speed were increasingly important as customers manage demanding production schedules and more complex orders.
“Our customers manage demanding production schedules and increasingly complex orders, so accuracy and speed are essential,” Hossain said.
“By improving visibility of stock and connecting packing, storage and dispatch more closely, the Smart Warehouse strengthens the service behind our apparel solutions and helps us respond more effectively as customers move towards shorter lead times and more customized production,” he said.
The Smart Warehouse will support apparel and footwear factories serving Bangladesh and global markets by improving inventory visibility and responsiveness while reducing picking delays and logistics errors.
The facility is part of Avery Dennison’s wider apparel solutions portfolio, including Embelex™, its apparel embellishment platform covering heat transfers, embroidered patches, woven labels and specialty graphics; Optica™, its end-to-end supply chain solutions portfolio; and radio-frequency identification (RFID) and other digital identification technologies.
Together, the solutions are designed to help brands and manufacturers create branded products, improve inventory visibility and strengthen traceability across production, distribution and retail.

item.title: Dengue: Eight more die as 1,733 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:

Of them, 701 patients were from Dhaka Division, 110 from Mymensingh Division, 191 from Chittagong Division, 302 from Khulna Division, 191 from Barisal Division, 145 from Rajshahi Division, 86 from Rangpur Division, and 7 from Sylhet Division.
A total of 53,570 patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country this year. Of them, 49,375 patients have recovered after receiving treatment at hospitals and have been discharged.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, while 413 people died from the disease last year.
